verification: Source tracing only. No compile, runtime test, publication or new product edit in this investigation step.
supported_counterexample: Existing native ancestor retains the same execution-console capability and can submit another Run16 DOS request while a descendant command is waiting.
CPU thread enters cmdExec32 -> GetNextVDMCommand; BaseSrvGetNextVDMCommand resets its wait event and releases the critical section.
Original cmdCreateProcess thread increments nReEntrancy via Client_Reenter and returns from that RPC before reading getSS/getBP. It may be scheduled out at this ordinary instruction boundary.

Another inherited-context Run16 request reaches OpenNtBaseServiceCheck; BaseSrvDOSWorkerWaitPending sees the reset event and admits reuse. Busy CheckDOS creates VDM_TO_TAKE_A_COMMAND and signals the event because nReEntrancy is nonzero.

Waiting CPU thread retries GetNextVDMCommand, consumes the other command and returns CF=1 from cmdExec32; guest execution may change registers before original cmdCreateProcess resumes its getSS/getBP reads.
No lock spans increment -> input consumption, and child CREATE_SUSPENDED does not constrain this independent ancestor request.
decision_scope: Source proof justifies preserving pre-reentry input ownership; it does not prove all snapshot functions, shared conversion, service tags or their current size necessary. R0021 initialization is retained for owner decision while its fallible snapshot consumer remains. Full original asynchronous access is not proposed as safe.
minimum_option: Keep the existing one-line initialization with the fallible consumer; do not introduce another mechanism. Review the coupled consumer and conversion separately for reductions.
